blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Same key on retry, ==never retry a decline==, never move state backwards, and ledger debits must equal credits.

blocks.q: The PSP call times out after 5 s. The retry code below runs on each attempt. Spot the bug.
a_bullets: The key is generated per attempt, so the PSP sees two different charges.
If the first call actually succeeded, the customer is charged twice.
Generate the key once per payment intent and send the same key on every retry.
A timeout means the outcome is UNKNOWN, so the retry must reuse the key (or query the PSP first).

blocks.q: A payment is already CAPTURED when a delayed AUTHORIZED webhook arrives. What is the status afterwards?
a_bullets: The status stays CAPTURED, because state never moves backwards.
The late event is applied idempotently as a no-op.
It is logged in payment_events for the audit trail.
It is not counted as an illegal-transition rejection, because that metric signals bugs or racing writers.

blocks.q: A capture of 100.00 posts: debit PSP Clearing 100.00, credit Merchant Revenue 100.00, credit Fees Payable 2.90. What is wrong, and how is it caught?
a_bullets: Debits total 100.00 but credits total 102.90, so the entries are unbalanced.
Revenue should be 97.10, so that credits 97.10 + 2.90 = 100.00.
Posting runs as one DB transaction that rejects any txn where sum(debits) != sum(credits).
The imbalance alert fires on any nonzero value, since the target is always 0.

blocks.q: A 100.00 payment is CAPTURED. A 60.00 refund has succeeded, and now a 50.00 refund request arrives. What happens?
a_bullets: It is rejected: 60 + 50 = 110, which is more than the 100.00 captured.
The check sum(refunds) <= captured runs inside a DB transaction, so two racing requests cannot both pass.
A refund of 40.00 or less would still be allowed, since partial refunds are fine.
Each refund carries its own idempotency key, so a retried 60.00 request is not refunded twice.

blocks.q: Key K was used for a 100.00 payment. The same key K now arrives with an amount of 120.00. What is returned?
a_bullets: 422, because the stored request_hash differs from the new request's hash.
The stored response is not replayed, since this is a different request, not a duplicate.
A concurrent duplicate with the identical body would get 409 while the first is still IN_PROGRESS.
An identical body after completion gets the stored response replayed.
